_status: COMPLETE: all THREE legs (JS, Python, native Kotlin) have now actually been run and compared. The native leg was compiled and executed on a real Android emulator on 2026-09-22; it is no longer untested source. See native_leg below.
_no_calibration_claim: median_r/g/b below are raw pixel statistics of a synthetic fixture image, not any water-quality/safety threshold or calibrated measurement.

fixture.description: Synthetic 90x120 JPEG (quality=90). Content is a solid-color quadrilateral (120,40,200) on a dark background, physically stored pre-rotated 90deg CCW with EXIF Orientation=6 set, so a spec-correct reader must EXIF-correct it back to the 120x90 upright frame to recover the known ROI at the known corners. Not a real camera photo - see docs/agent-workflow/handoff-T04.md for why.

native_leg.command: npx expo run:android  (then apps/mobile/src/nativeGolden.ts runs on app start; result read from `adb logcat` tag T04_NATIVE_GOLDEN)

result.time_note: 5 timed runs after one discarded warm-up. The 651 ms outlier is first-call class loading/JIT; the median is the representative figure.

process_memory.source: adb shell dumpsys meminfo org.jalsakshi.mobile (whole RN app process, NOT the feature computation alone)
process_memory.caveat: Process-level figure. It is not a per-call allocation measurement and must not be compared directly with the JS heap delta or Python peak below.

device.model: sdk_gphone64_x86_64 (Android emulator, NOT a physical phone)

comparison.native_vs_python: EXACT MATCH on all fields, including median_r/g/b (120/40/201).
comparison.native_vs_js: median_r/g/b differ by exactly 1 per channel (native 120/40/201 vs js 119/39/200). Orientation, ROI size, sample_count and upright dimensions all agree exactly.
comparison.root_cause_of_the_js_difference: Confirmed, not assumed. T04 originally recorded a +/-1 per channel JS/Python gap and attributed it to a cross-decoder rounding difference (jpeg-js vs Pillow/libjpeg). The native leg decodes with Android BitmapFactory, which is also libjpeg-based, and it matches Python EXACTLY. That is direct evidence the outlier is the jpeg-js decoder, not the shared algorithm: two independent libjpeg-based decoders agree to the bit, and only the pure-JS decoder differs.
comparison.agreement_verdict: Three-way agreement holds on every structural field (schema_version, roi size, sample_count, orientation_read, upright dimensions). Colour medians agree exactly between native and Python; JS is within the previously measured +/-1 per channel decoder tolerance.
